_about: Public-domain John Eliot (1604-1690), pastor of Roxbury and missionary to the Massachusett, for the Word Hoard: the Indian tracts (Tears of Repentance 1653, A Late and Further Manifestation 1655, the Further Accounts of 1659 and 1660, the Brief Narrative of 1671), The Christian Commonwealth (1659), Communion of Churches (1665), The Indian Grammar Begun (1666), Indian Dialogues (1671), The Harmony of the Gospels (1678), A Brief Answer on infant baptism (1679), The Dying Speeches of Several Indians (1683), the Logic Primer (1672, reprinted 1904) and his letters to Jonathan Hanmer (1915), from Internet Archive scans. His Massachusett Bible and translations are left out as not English. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 39 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

_excluded.eliot-not-english: The Massachusett Bible (1663, 1685) and New Testament (1661), the Indian Primers (1669, 1687, 1720, 1747, 1877, 1880) and his Massachusett translations of Bayly and Shepard: not English
